title: The invisible war: Iran's evolving cyberattacks bring battlefront to small-town America
content: The escalation of Iran's cyber capabilities in its ongoing tensions with the US and Israel is becoming increasingly pronounced. Recent intrusions into US water facilities mark a transition into a new blend of warfare. These digital strikes bolster military initiatives while attempting to sway international public opinion. Additionally, the infusion of artificial intelligence into these operations allows for unprecedented efficiency and breadth, reinforcing Iran's asymmetric strategies within its military doctrine.

title: 'Being Pullela Gopichand's daughter is a big baggage': Coach B Sumeeth Reddy
content: Player-turned-coach Sumeeth Reddy says Gayatri Gopichand's maiden World Championships medal is more than a podium finish. It's the release of years of expectation carried as the daughter of Indian badminton legend and national coach Pullela Gopichand. The team of Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly defeated China's Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 to secure at least a bronze.

title: Maharashtra teen jumps off cliff, parents fall to death trying to save him
content: A family of three tragically died after falling into a deep stone quarry on Friday. The incident occurred when parents attempted to save their son from a dangerous cliff edge. Police and fire brigade personnel were present and had been trying to persuade the youth for hours. The son suddenly fell, and his father tried to grab him, losing his own balance.

title: Zuckerberg buys Gothic castle in Ireland, Meta's international HQ, for $35 mn
content: Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, and his wife, Priscilla Chan, have acquired the historic Strancally Castle, a stunning Gothic mansion set on an expansive estate in Ireland. This remarkable property will serve as their home base during visits to the nation, which is significant due to Meta's international headquarters being located there. The couple is excited about the opportunity to preserve and nurture this piece of history.

title: FDA shuts Radio Club, Khar Gymkhana, McDonald's Colaba kitchens over hygiene violations
content: The FDA has temporarily revoked licenses for The Bombay Presidency Radio Club and Khar Gymkhana, citing poor waste management and pest control. The kitchen at The Bombay Presidency Radio Club was notably infested with flies and included dead cockroaches, while a live cockroach issue led to a similar suspension for McDonald's Colaba. These measures highlight serious breaches of hygiene and food safety regulations.

title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal gives an update on Temple device
content: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal revealed the Temple wearable device is now smaller and more powerful.  Pre-orders for the limited launch edition will begin very soon.  The device is expected to ship before the end of 2026.  PV Sindhu was recently seen wearing the Temple device at a championship.  This device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain.

title: Congress’s renewed youth outreach: How CJP has forced parties to course correct
content: Student protests at Jantar Mantar have prompted political parties to rethink their youth engagement strategies. The Congress party is now focusing on youth issues and expanding its outreach programs nationwide. Rahul Gandhi's recent actions highlight the party's renewed commitment to addressing student concerns. The Congress Working Committee has proposed an education-to-employment roadmap for young people. This shift reflects a broader effort to regain support among the nation's youth.

title: English town builds swing bridge with recycled plastic bottles in its deck
content: A vibrant addition to an English town's landscape, a six-meter swing bridge constructed from recycled plastic bottles has just been unveiled. This bridge, which opens manually for river traffic, is integral to a multi-million-pound project aimed at restoring the Wilts & Berks Canal and establishing a public 600-meter stretch of waterway. Its completion represents a bold step toward enhancing local heritage.

title: Chicago mayor bulldozed airport runway in 2003; site later became nature park
content: Chicago's Meigs Field airport was controversially closed overnight in 2003.  Six X-shaped gouges rendered the runway unusable, stranding sixteen aircraft.  The city cited security concerns following the September 11 attacks for the closure.  Twelve years later, the former airfield became a natural landscape.  This site now features prairie, wetlands, and wildlife habitat for migratory birds.

title: Apple 'fires' entire VR team as John Ternus takes over as CEO from Tim Cook
content: Apple has laid off at least 60 employees tied to its VR development team, with an entire group working on virtual reality reportedly cut just days before John Ternus takes over as CEO on September 1. The move comes as Apple shifts resources toward Siri AI and smart glasses, leaving Apple Vision Pro, the $3,699 headset Tim Cook once called "tomorrow's technology today," with a visibly shrinking team behind it.

title: Harry and Meghan's California mansion may be sold as couple weighs return to Britain
content: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are contemplating selling their lavish Montecito mansion as the financial burden of over $600,000 annually in mortgage and property taxes weighs heavily. Initially purchased for $14.65 million, the estate is generating buzz among brokers, with potential sale prices estimated between $55 million and $65 million. A final decision may follow their relocation to the UK.

title: India new ‘swing supplier’ for refined oil products. Can it sustain?
content: Oil products now account for a much larger share of India's exports to several destinations. India has about 258.1 million tonnes of installed refining capacity across 23 refineries. It is the fourth-largest refining centre globally after the US, China and Russia.

title: Arjun Rampal marries his girlfriend Gabriella Demetriades in Goa
content: On Friday, Arjun Rampal and Gabriella Demetriades took a significant step in their relationship by registering their marriage in Goa. This took place at the Sub-Registrar's office in Mapusa, where they were granted special permission to skip the usual 15-day waiting period. The couple, who have been together since 2018 and share two sons, celebrated their engagement in a prior podcast episode.

title: Strawberry tells Kyrgios: Talent isn't enough, you need healing inside, not punishment
content: Darryl Strawberry advocates for Nick Kyrgios' support after a cocaine positive test.  He believes substance abuse issues require healing, not just punishment.  Strawberry, a former baseball star, understands the immense public pressure athletes face.  He hopes Kyrgios receives care and time to recover from his struggles.  This approach, he suggests, is more effective than solely focusing on penalties.

title: Savinho's record $115M move to Spurs boosts De Zerbi's attack overhaul
content: Tottenham Hotspur has agreed an eighty-five million pound deal for Manchester City winger Savinho.  The Brazilian international is expected to undergo his medical on Friday afternoon.  Savinho has struggled for consistent first-team football at Manchester City since joining.  Tottenham are also negotiating a separate deal for striker Omar Marmoush with City.  This move signifies Tottenham's significant summer investment in their squad.

title: Verstappen's new Red Bull deal through 2030 reportedly worth €460M
content: Max Verstappen has signed a contract extension with Red Bull Racing until 2030.  This decision ends months of speculation regarding his future team.  Reportedly, the deal includes a significant financial commitment from the team.  Verstappen expressed comfort and a desire to continue winning with Red Bull.  The team now aims to build a competitive car for future seasons.

title: Joe Root creates history in Headingly against Pakistan
content: In a remarkable achievement, Joe Root has eclipsed Steve Smith to become the foremost fielder for Test cricket catches. This significant milestone was celebrated with a crisp catch at leg slip during the opening Test. With a strategic bowling effort, England's attack secured Root's record-breaking moment, allowing the team to establish a commanding lead against Pakistan in the match, further embellishing Root's impressive cricket legacy.

title: 1 dead, 3 injured after building collapses during demolition work in Karol Bagh

Preliminary inquiries suggest the building owners lacked necessary demolition permits from authorities. Rescue operations were launched by police and fire services after local residents alerted them. The building owners and the contractor have been detained for questioning regarding the collapse.

title: Pakistan's Ali Usman creates history, ends 16-year wait in England
content: Usman was Pakistan's standout bowler. He finished with 5/95 from 24 overs and claimed his first five-wicket haul in England. The left-arm spinner also became the first visiting left-arm spinner since Shakib Al Hasan in 2010 to take five wickets in a Test innings in England. Usman was also the first visiting spinner to take a five-wicket haul at Leeds since Australia's Ashley Mallett took 5/114 in 1972.

title: Who pays what in a rental home? Property tax, maintenance and utility bills explained
content: In India, property taxes are fundamentally the responsibility of the property owner as per municipal regulations. Meanwhile, utility expenses for water and electricity are usually settled by the tenant who consumes these services. Maintenance fees of housing societies are generally charged to owners, but tenancy agreements can sometimes allocate part of these costs to renters. Clarifying these responsibilities helps avoid conflicts between landlords and tenants.

title: 'Programme not appropriate': MEA on no clearance for Telangana CM's US visit

However, he has secured clearance for his trip to the UK. As a result, the Chief Minister's office confirmed the cancellation of the US portion, prompting an earlier return to Hyderabad than originally planned.

title: Why short-range ballistic missiles are the new weapon of choice, and how Pralay stands out
content: Modern conflicts highlight the challenge of intercepting short-range ballistic missiles effectively.  Russia and Iran have extensively used such weapons in recent warfare.  India's Pralay missile offers battlefield flexibility and operates outside nuclear doctrine.  This missile features terminal maneuverability and a solid-fuel propulsion system.  Pralay's capabilities position it as a leading short-range ballistic missile globally.

title: BJP claims influencers were offered Rs 25,000 to attend Rahul Gandhi's Pune event

Several nations are now seeking to acquire this advanced supersonic cruise missile.  The Philippines, Vietnam, and Indonesia have already signed deals for the weapon.  Further interest from countries in the Gulf and Southeast Asia is growing.

This meeting is prompted by a notable rise in swine flu cases due to unstable weather conditions. Health officials will evaluate healthcare preparedness and devise containment strategies. The primary objective is to enhance surveillance and ensure hospitals are fully equipped to curb the virus's spread in the city.

title: 'No credibility': India slams US religious freedom body over call for RSS sanctions
content: the ministry of external affairs hits back at the united states commission on international religious freedom . the commission says such organisations have no credibility and operate to peddle their own agenda . this comes days after the USCIRF urged the US government to impose sanctions on RSS members .

title: ‘Received no help’: Odisha man’s body kept on rooftop for 18 hours amid floods
content: the body of a 61-year-old man remained on the rooftop of his flooded home for nearly 18 hours . the incident took place in Chintasahi under bari panchayat . several families have remained surrounded by floodwaters for six days .
